The in-flight reading is established in the download-delete and interrupted-recovery cases, which hold a transfer at the source barrier and compare the rendered bar against the reported bytes.

covered by this case for the server-failure half: the source returns a real 503 and the same row's public Retry is used, with the original node and storage resubmitted in the request body, so a retry is a retry of that row and not a second resource. The transfer records for this run carry status, planned_bytes and sha256_sent per request, so the accepted request is matched against bytes actually sent rather than against a 2xx alone.

Both clauses are proven, in the same run. First clause: a real transfer is started to an owned local storage from the model detail Download to dialog and the source is held mid-response, so the row is genuinely downloading with real bytes on disk. The page's own row-level Cancel download control is used: it opens the presenceAction.cancelDownloadConfirm popconfirm, and confirming it is asserted to send exactly one POST /api/v1/models/{id}/download/cancel carrying storage_id and node_uuid and nothing else, answered 200 with state canceled. The presenceMessage.downloadCanceled toast appears, the row renders the presence.canceled label together with the row reason, and an independent GET of the model agrees on state canceled, acquisition download and the message Download canceled by user. The bytes already reported are neither zeroed nor inflated to the finished total by the withdrawal, so the row cannot pass the cancel off as a completed transfer. Termination is asserted against the task and not against the label: the source's held response is then torn down under the agent, and for a five second window afterwards the source receives no further request at all, while the row stays canceled. The temporary resource is asserted too: the resumable weight-name .part file survives the cancel at the exact full weight size carrying payload bytes while the finished weight file does not exist, which is what the confirm text promises for a retry. The temporary resource is further pinned to real data: the chunk writer preallocates the full size and fills chunks out of order, so every byte the transfer did write is compared against the source payload at that same offset and any mismatch would fail the case, which rules out a sparse hole being passed off as a resume point. Proven by mutation: the withdrawal was made label-only by removing the writer stop call and by no longer pausing the task for a canceled row, and the cancel test then failed with AssertionError: the canceled transfer kept asking the source for bytes: ... range bytes=1638466-2097239 ... so the five second window is not a tautology and the canceled row cannot be relabelled while the transfer keeps running. Finally the row is reclaimed and the eviction answers a physical byte count equal to the count the canceled row reported, so the kept data is accounted for. Second clause: the pre-submit Download to dialog is reopened and Cancel, Escape, close cross and mask are each taken with zero POST /download requests and no file row created, so closing the dialog is a dialog dismissal and not a task cancellation; this is asserted separately from the row cancel above.
covered: the detail is reopened after a refresh and still shows the file row, and the independent GET agrees, so progress is not reset to zero or shown complete before the bytes landed.

covered for the files this case transfers: every synthetic payload byte and its sha256 are read back at an independent agent root, so the final file is verified rather than assumed. Tensor inference consuming the artifact stays with the inference cases.

Partial: only the download side applies to this surface, and this case proves both halves of it. Bytes and format: each delivered file on the actual chosen path is decoded through its own standard envelope - config.json by Python's json module, model.safetensors by the length-prefixed header the safetensors format defines - and the sha256 of the bytes on disk equals the sha256 of the bytes the external repository served, so the format claim rests on the format itself and not on the product's serializer, and completion leaves exactly the source file set beside the product's own completion marker with no .part, .tmp or .html leftover. Failure clause, which is this case's specialty: the weight source really answers 503, and then the storage directory is enumerated and every file in it is compared to the served bytes and to the fixture's real error body - the fixture's root route is fetched first and really answers a 241-byte text/html table, and both declared file names are fed that body and must be rejected by the HTML detector, so the check is calibrated rather than vacuously clean; after the real 503 only config.json remains at byte-identical source content, with no substitute file and no error page stored as the model file, and the retry that follows reaches the same verification. The remaining sub-dimensions are export-shaped and are NOT claimed: 中文编码, 列/单位, 记录数与筛选一致 need an exported artifact, and this page has none - neither models locale file contains any word for export, ui/src/pages/models has no export surface, the tables declare no antd filter or sorter, and the backend exposes no model export route. That half belongs to the logs export contract, declared there by log-filter-export.json; claiming it here would be a mis-attribution, so this item remains a gap in the completion queue.
